title: Percutaneous approach to aortic disease: EVAR, TEVAR and newer techniques for more proximal disease.
abstract: Advances in device design, imaging and vascular-closure technology have driven a progressive shift from surgical femoral exposure to totally percutaneous strategies for endovascular aortic repair. This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. Percutaneous femoral access is now supported by randomized evidence, large registries and administrative cohorts showing high technical success, fewer wound complications, shorter operative times and shorter hospital stay compared with routine surgical cutdown, and real-time ultrasound-guided puncture has become a guideline-endorsed standard of care. Major contemporary developments include computed tomography-based access planning centred on calcification burden and sheath-to-artery ratio; an individualised, anatomy-driven choice between suture- and plug-based closure devices; endovascular preparation of hostile iliofemoral anatomy with pave-and-crack, endoconduits and intravascular lithotripsy; low-profile endografts that have widened transfemoral eligibility; and percutaneous axillary and carotid routes that enable complex TEVAR, fenestrated/branched and selected arch repairs in experienced centres, although evidence for these latter applications remains largely observational. Looking ahead, further reductions in delivery-system profile, dedicated large-bore closure technologies, image-fusion guidance and off-the-shelf branched devices are expected to extend fully percutaneous repair to increasingly complex anatomy, while prospective, aortic-specific and device-level comparisons with standardized anatomical metrics and long-term follow-up are needed to refine patient selection and confirm durable limb and target-vessel patency.

This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: NON-INVASIVE HemodynamicS of Non-Thrombotic Iliac Vein Lesions ARE DISTURBED IN PATIEnTS with A HiSTORY OF Deep Venous Thrombosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05. RESULTS: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device.

title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Admission C-Reactive Protein-to-Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Early Major Amputation After Minor Amputation in Patients With Infected Foot Wounds.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810). CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification. LEVEL OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE: Level III.

title: Feasibility, Safety and Efficacy of Outpatient Lipoabdominoplasty with Sedation, TAP Block, and Tumescent Anesthesia.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Postoperative pain after abdominoplasty can reduce patient satisfaction, delay mobility, and increase complications like deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Multimodal analgesia, including transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks, improves pain control, reduces opioid use, improving recovery, minimizing DVT risks, and promoting early ambulation and recovery. OBJECTIVE: This article examines the safety, effectiveness, and practical aspects of abdominoplasty under sedation and TAP block as an alternative to general anesthesia, detailing the anesthetic protocol and patient outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center case series encompassed all consecutive lipoabdominoplasty patients from December 2020 to June 2025. Epidemiology, procedures, medications, patient-reported outcomes, satisfaction, and complications were collected via standardized questionnaires, including BodyQ, Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS) and International Pain Outcome (IPO) questionnaire. RESULTS: Forty patients (mean age 37 ± 11) underwent lipoabdominoplasty under conscious sedation and TAP-block; 45% also underwent breast surgery. During the first 24 postoperative hours, 31% of patients experienced at least one episode of severe pain, lasting a cumulative average of 2.4 hours. 90% reported minimal/no nausea. No antiemetics were required; 25% received one opioid dose. Analgesia satisfaction was 90%. Median discharge time was 2:42 h (interquartile range [IQR] 2:00-3:16). Appearance satisfaction was 100% (IQR 81-100%). CONCLUSION: Lipoabdominoplasty with sedation, TAP block, and tumescent anesthesia can be safely performed in the outpatient setting, with minimal to no nausea, low to moderate pain, and great patient satisfaction. The evidence supports revisiting postoperative care pathways to ensure prudent utilization of hospital assets, like minimizing unnecessary inpatient observation, without compromising outcomes.Level of Evidence: IV.

title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma.
abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: 2 P ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R= 0.72;< 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: P P Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21];=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

title: Predictors of Surveillance Imaging Non-compliance Among Patients with TEVAR for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
abstract: P P ObjectivesBlunt Thoracic Aortic Injury (BTAI) is the second leading cause of death for patients with blunt trauma. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has become the standard of care for high-grade BTAI, reducing morbidity and mortality while requiring long-term surveillance imaging to ensure graft integrity and prevent future complications. However, adherence to this protocol is poor. Previous studies evaluating the factors associated with post-operative imaging non-compliance have yielded conflicting results. This study aimed to evaluate predictors of post-TEVAR non-compliance inpatients presenting with BTAI.MethodsA retrospective study on 23 patients was conducted using a single institution Aortic Center Database (2015-2025). Inclusion criteria included patients who were age >18 years and underwent TEVAR for BTAI. Demographic, comorbidity, hospital course, and follow-up data were collected. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) score was derived from patient's home address ZIP code. Time-to-event analysis defined loss to follow up (LTFU) for vascular imaging as the failure event. Patients were censored at death or if compliant through 1 year following the index TEVAR. Statistical analysis included chi-square, t-tests, and Kaplan-Meier survival.ResultsBased on this single-center review on TEVAR follow-up for BTAI, sex, race, and hospital length of stay did not impact compliance. Medical comorbidities were also non-significant. Patients who presented with a lower injury severity score (= 0.02) and lived more than 20 miles from their follow-up appointment (= 0.02) were more likely to be LTFU. While the type of facility was not impactful, all patients who were discharged to a non-home location were LTFU. Interestingly, DCI and insurance status had no impact on follow-up non-compliance.ConclusionsThis study supports the development of targeted, patient-centered surveillance strategies, especially amongst rural populations and those discharged to a non-home location. To fully understand this complex problem, further investigation using a larger database may be indicated.

title: Trans-Patch Retrograde Re-Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re-Entry Strategies.
abstract: Failure of true-lumen re-entry after subintimal wire passage is a well-recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73-year-old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans-patch retrograde access and dedicated device-assisted re-entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12-month follow-up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6-month follow-up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re-entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.

Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality.

title: Outcomes After Major Amputation in Octogenarians.
abstract: BackgroundMajor lower extremity amputations, defined as above-ankle amputations, are morbid and significantly life-changing. Older patients may be more susceptible to poor outcomes. Our goal was to assess the short- and long-term outcomes of major amputations in octogenarians.MethodsA retrospective single-center chart review was performed on all octogenarian patients who underwent a major amputation at a safety-net hospital between 2014-2023. Demographics, operative characteristics, postoperative outcomes, and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were collected and analyzed. Multivariable binary logistic regression evaluated factors associated with 1-year mortality. Fisher's exact test evaluated univariate categorical comparisons because of small cell frequencies.Results56 octogenarian patients underwent a major amputation: 96.4% underwent an amputation for chronic limb-threatening ischemia while 3.6% of patients had acute limb ischemia. Above-knee and below-knee amputations accounted for 73.2 and 26.8% of procedures, respectively; 10.6% were guillotine amputations. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 26.3% of cases, and total mean hospital length of stay (LOS) was 13.7 days. Postoperatively, 55.4% were discharged to a skilled nursing facility, 17.9% patients to an acute rehab facility, and 12.5% to home with assistance. Thirty-day emergency department use rate was 14.3%, and hospital readmission rate was 12.5%. Most patients (83.9%) were non-ambulatory at 1-year. In-hospital mortality was 8.9%, 30-day mortality was 14.3%, and 1-year mortality was 35.7%. Univariate analyses demonstrated no statistically significant differences among evaluated variables. Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was also not statistically significant.ConclusionMajor amputations in octogenarians are highly morbid with high ICU utilization and prolonged LOS with frequent discharge to acute care facilities. About one-third of patients are not alive at 1-year. These findings suggest the need to identify opportunities for improvement in this high-risk patient population undergoing amputations, such as early revascularization, aggressive rehabilitation in concert with geriatrician collaboration, medical optimization, and improved goals-of-care discussions.

Our goal was to assess the short- and long-term outcomes of major amputations in octogenarians.MethodsA retrospective single-center chart review was performed on all octogenarian patients who underwent a major amputation at a safety-net hospital between 2014-2023.

title: MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) Variant Associated With Hereditary Thoracic Aortic Diseases and Early Onset Aortic Dissection.
abstract: AIMS: Thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections are major causes of sudden cardiovascular death. We aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of the MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant in Finnish families with heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) and to assess evidence for a potential founder effect. METHODS: We evaluated the clinical significance and potential founder effect of the missense variant MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) in Finnish families. Eight individuals from four unrelated Finnish families carrying the MYLK c.4079G>A heterozygous variant were recruited. Clinical histories, imaging data, and pedigrees were reviewed. Genetic testing included exome‑based gene panel sequencing or targeted familial variant testing. Variant classification followed the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics 2015 guidelines. RESULTS: Thoracic aortic dilatation or aneurysm occurred in 6/8 carriers (75%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 45 years (range 34-67). Ascending aortic diameters ranged from 26-59 mm, most often measured at the aortic root. Aortic dissection occurred in 4/8 (50%) at a mean age of 46 years (range 34-68), including three early‑adult events. Extrathoracic arterial involvement (carotid) was observed in one variant‑positive individual. CONCLUSION: The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant was present in six affected individuals from four unrelated families and is enriched in the Finnish population, supporting a founder effect. The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant is associated with early‑adult‑onset, high‑penetrance thoracic aortic disease and substantial dissection risk, underscoring the need for vigilant surveillance and early intervention in affected individuals and at‑risk relatives.

We aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of the MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant in Finnish families with heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) and to assess evidence for a potential founder effect. METHODS: We evaluated the clinical significance and potential founder effect of the missense variant MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) in Finnish families.

title: [Risk prediction of pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the risk factors for pneumonia after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) infection in maintenance hemodialysis patients from a single center in China, and to establish a multivariate model to predict the risk of pneumonia. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected. Multivariate Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were adopted to explore risk factors of pneumonia, and a multivariate model was established to predict the risk of pneumonia occurrence. RESULTS: vs. P vs. P vs. P vs. P vs. P vs. P vs. P OR CI P OR CI P OR CI P CI P A total of 209 hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection were enrolled, including 80 patients (38.3%) with pneumonia and 129 patients (61.7%) without pneumonia. Compared with the non-pneumonia group, the pneumonia group presented a significantly higher mean age [(65.8±13.7) years(58.9±12.6) years,< 0.001] and elevated C-reactive protein levels [4.58(1.62, 9.99) mg/L2.35(0.95, 6.50) mg/L,=0.007]. In contrast, the pneumonia group had markedly lower hemoglobin [(109±15) g/L(116±11) g/L,=0.001], serum phosphorus [(1.60±0.52) mmol/L(1.78±0.53) mmol/L,=0.022], serum albumin [(35.9±4.1) g/L(38.6±2.5) g/L,< 0.001], arteriovenous fistula utilization rate (81.3%96.9%,< 0.001), and single dialysis session duration [(232±14) min(236±11) min,=0.046]. Multivariate Logistic analysis revealed that advanced age (=1.030, 95%: 1.002-1.059,=0.036), lower hemoglobin (=0.968, 95%: 0.942-0.995,=0.019), lower albumin (=0.834, 95%: 0.738-0.943,=0.004) were independent risk factors for pneumonia. Patients over 65 years old, with hemoglobin < 115 g/L or serum albumin < 36.8 g/L had elevated risk of pneumonia. A combined predictive factor Q composed of these three indicators was developed for risk prediction of pneumonia. We drew the ROC curve with the predictive factor Q [area under the curve (AUC) =0.756, 95%: 0.687-0.825,< 0.001]. Taking the cut-off value of 0.575, the sensitivity and specificity of predictive factor Q for predicting pneumonia were 44.0% and 94.5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Advanced age, anemia and hypoalbuminemia are risk factors for pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection. A predictive marker Q value less than 0.575 indicates low risk of pneumonia, which can be applied for rapid risk stratification among hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Coil Embolization and Open Splenectomy for a Massive Splenic Vein Aneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic vein aneurysms (SVAs) are a rare vascular anomaly of the portal system that are often asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging. Intervention is reserved for aneurysms that are enlarging, thrombosed, symptomatic, or ruptured to avoid catastrophic complications. This can range from endovascular to open, complex procedures. Here, we present the case of a massive, symptomatic, partially thrombosed SVA that required a hybrid approach involving both minimally invasive and open surgery. CASE PRESENTATION: A 56-year-old woman presented to the emergency department for an infected right foot wound and was admitted for intravenous antibiotics and surgical debridement. While hospitalized, she had a worsening transaminitis with associated abdominal pain, prompting investigation with a computed tomography (CT) scan, which identified a massively dilated, partially thrombosed SVA measuring 18 cm. Given the enormous size of the aneurysm and substantial risk of impending rupture, urgent surgical intervention was planned. Preoperative coil embolization of the splenic artery was performed first to reduce the arterial inflow to the SVA and to minimize the risk of intraoperative hemorrhage during open resection. Three days after embolization, the patient underwent open splenectomy with aneurysmectomy for definitive management. The patient's postoperative course was complicated by a bleeding gastric ulcer that was successfully cauterized, and she was discharged home on postoperative Day 10 after receiving the recommended postsplenectomy vaccines. CONCLUSION: No standard treatment algorithm exists for SVAs, as management is individualized, and treatment evidence is limited to case reports and series. This patient had one of the largest SVAs ever recorded, and management was based on the acuity of symptoms, size, and rupture risk of the aneurysm sac. This case also demonstrated the success of a novel management approach to massive SVAs, using preoperative embolization of the splenic artery followed by open resection without portal reconstruction.

title: Multistage Preclinical Evaluation of MRI-Guided Stenting for Coarctation of the Aorta using in vitro and Porcine Models.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models. RESULTS: All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept. CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T.

title: Unintended Shifts in High-Priority Adult Heart Transplant Listings after the OPTN's September 2025 Policy Change.
abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024-June 2025, n=4,206) and post-policy (September 2025-June 2026, n=4,231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024-June 2025, n=4,206) and post-policy (September 2025-June 2026, n=4,231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001).

title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies. METHODS: st th A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1, 2005, to August 6, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies.

title: Plasma Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population. AIM: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2- and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations. RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs. lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR 3.87, 95% CI 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR: 1.51, 95% CI: 0.82-2.80). CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

AIM: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007).

title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2- positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with JAK2V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IR) per 100 person-years (PY) and incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing aspirin use versus no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n=1,760 with aspirin, n=367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in JAK2V617F-positive MPN patients receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 PY (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59 - 4.65; I=93%) with pooled IRR receiving aspirin versus no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI 0.40 - 0.86, I=16%). The pooled IR of major and non-major bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI 1.06 - 3.65; I=90%) per 100 PY with pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI 1.15 - 5.11; I=43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence the better define the role of aspirin in JAK2V617F-positive MPNs.

title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI. METHODS: This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed. RESULTS: p p p p A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%;= 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986;= 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250;= 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894;= 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874). CONCLUSION: Foot microcirculation differed significantly between patients with Cla and CLTI on CTP. Hb, TTP, and BF were independent predictors for CLTI. All models demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with model C yielding the highest AUC. CLINICALTRIALS: gov Identifier:NCT05575778.

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well. METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates. RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation. CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

title: Impact of Insurance Type on Timing of Diagnosis and Surgical Treatment of Acute Achilles Tendon Ruptures: A 2-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: III Introduction/PurposeDelayed treatment of acute Achilles tendon rupture is associated with worse outcomes and higher complication rates. Prior studies suggest reduced access to care among Medicaid and uninsured patients. This study examines the effect of insurance status on the timing of diagnosis and surgical treatment among patients undergoing surgical repair of acute Achilles tendon rupture.MethodsA retrospective chart review was conducted of patients aged ≥18 years with acute traumatic Achilles tendon ruptures identified by Current Procedural Terminology codes 27650 and 27654 at 2 hospitals between January 2017 and December 2023. Dates of injury, emergency department presentation, initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation, and surgical intervention were recorded. Only patients who ultimately underwent operative repair were eligible for inclusion; because case ascertainment relied on surgical procedure codes, the cohort does not capture patients managed nonoperatively or those who never reached surgical care. Insurance status was categorized as private or Medicaid/uninsured. Postoperative complications, including re-rupture, infection, venous thromboembolism, wound dehiscence, return to the operating room, and mortality, were documented. Between-group comparisons of continuous variables were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, given non-normal distribution of the underlying data; independent 2-tailed t-tests were performed as a secondary, confirmatory analysis. Significance was set at P < .05.ResultsThirty-eight surgically treated patients met the inclusion criteria, including 23 with private insurance and 15 who were Medicaid or uninsured. Median age was 35.2 years, and 89.5% were male. All time intervals are reported as medians. Time from injury to emergency department presentation was longer in the Medicaid/uninsured group but not statistically significant (1.0 vs 0.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .079). Medicaid/uninsured patients experienced significantly longer delays from injury to initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation (17.0 vs 4.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .024) and from injury to surgery (30.0 vs 10.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .045). Time from orthopaedic evaluation to surgery did not differ significantly between groups (11.0 vs 6.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .206). Postoperative complications were infrequent in both groups; the study was not powered for comparison of complication rates and none was performed.ConclusionAmong surgically treated patients, those with Medicaid or no insurance experienced significantly longer delays to initial orthopaedic evaluation and to surgical repair compared with privately insured patients, highlighting disparities in access to timely orthopaedic care within this surgically treated population.Level of Evidence:.

title: Arabidopsis Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in.
abstract: Arabidopsis thaliana 34 It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using, we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that Uthiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant's interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

title: Taohong Siwu Decoction-Based Targeted Drug Penetration Therapy for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Hip Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Postoperative lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a common complication after hip fracture surgery, and complementary strategies targeting coagulation, inflammation, and venous circulation may provide additional preventive benefits. This retrospective cohort study included 86 patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between June 2023 and June 2024. Patients were assigned to a control group (n = 43), receiving standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis, or an observation group (n = 43), receiving additional Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy. The primary outcome was postoperative lower limb DVT within 10 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included coagulation parameters, inflammatory markers, femoral venous blood flow velocities, postoperative pain, limb swelling, and treatment-related adverse events. DVT occurred in 1/43 patients (2.33%) in the observation group and 10/43 patients (23.26%) in the control group (Fisher's exact P = 0.007). In a parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age and baseline D-dimer, adjunctive therapy remained associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative DVT (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.68, P = 0.017). After 10 days of treatment, the observation group had lower Faces Pain Scale-Revised scores and limb swelling, longer activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, lower D-dimer levels, higher common and superficial femoral vein blood flow velocities, and lower serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 levels than the control group (all P < 0.05). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in overall adverse-event occurrence, and no severe treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy combined with standard anticoagulation was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative DVT and favorable differences in coagulation, inflammatory, and venous hemodynamic parameters.

title: En bloc stapler versus separate clip ligation for renal hilar control during robotic-assisted nephrectomy: A retrospective comparative cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare en bloc endovascular stapler ligation (ENBLOC) with separate clip ligation (CLIPS) for renal hilar control during robotic-assisted nephrectomy, with emphasis on perioperative safety. PATIENTS AND METHODS: n n This single-centre retrospective cohort included 193 consecutive adults undergoing robotic-assisted radical nephrectomy, simple nephrectomy or nephroureterectomy between January 2018 and December 2025. Patients were classified as CLIPS ( = 66) or ENBLOC ( = 127). Primary safety outcomes were intraoperative complications, postoperative complications and postoperative arteriovenous fistula (AVF) formation. Operative, renal functional and oncological outcomes were secondary or exploratory. Procedure-specific subgroup analyses were also performed. RESULTS: p p p p p p Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, except for ASA III-IV status was more frequent in the CLIPS group (27.3% vs. 16.5%, = 0.029). Operative time (206.5 vs. 218.0 min, = 0.26), estimated blood loss (median 100 mL in both groups, = 0.37) and transfusion rates (1.5% vs. 5.5%, = 0.19) did not differ significantly. Intraoperative complications occurred in 3/66 (4.5%) CLIPS and 8/127 (6.3%) ENBLOC patients (OR 1.41, 95% CI 0.36-5.51; absolute risk difference 1.8 percentage points, 95% CI - 4.8 to 8.3; = 0.752). Postoperative complications occurred in 5/66 (7.6%) and 9/127 (7.1%) patients, respectively ( = 0.91). No AVF was identified during follow-up. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not identify additional statistically significant between-group differences, although estimates were limited by small sample sizes and sparse events. CONCLUSION: En bloc stapler ligation was not associated with statistically significant differences in the evaluated safety outcomes compared with separate clip ligation. However, the observational design and limited number of events preclude conclusions regarding equivalence, and clinically relevant differences cannot be excluded.

title: Perioperative Management of a Toddler With Tuberous Sclerosis and Dilated Cardiomyopathy Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Case Report.
abstract: Toddler abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are rare and lack defined perioperative guidelines. Aneurysms may be associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) but rarely occur with concurrent dilated cardiomyopathy. This case report describes the anesthetic and surgical considerations for a two-year-old male with TSC and dilated cardiomyopathy with low ejection fraction undergoing open infrarenal AAA repair. Our most important perioperative considerations included advanced hemodynamic monitoring, management of intraoperative blood loss, and the physiological changes associated with aortic clamping. Transesophageal echocardiography was used throughout the operation to guide inotropic support and assess ventricular filling using renal-protective strategies and balanced transfusion.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success.

title: Pre-Operative Ankle Brachial Index in Assessing Major Amputation Level and Outcomes in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: P BackgroundThe ankle brachial index (ABI) is a non-invasive tool used to assess vessel stenosis hindering limb perfusion. It is commonly used in diagnosis of peripheral artery disease (PAD). We propose that this diagnostic tool may have predictive applications in amputation level of patients with PAD and may contribute to the diagnostic evaluation of CLTI.Materials and MethodsThis study is a retrospective chart review of 97 patients with PAD admitted from 2014 to 2022 who underwent major lower extremity amputation (MLEA) at a major tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified into two groups by ABI severity (ABI ≤0.4: severe PAD, 0.4<ABI <0.9: less severe PAD). Statistical tests included Chi-square, T-test, multivariable logistic regression with collinearity statistics, and a receiver operator curve (ROC) to determine Youden's J.ResultsNinety-seven patients were included in this study, 53.6% (n = 52) of whom had less severe PAD and 46.4% (n = 45) of whom had severe PAD. Per multivariable logistic regression, more severe PAD based on ABI ≤0.4 was predictive of receiving an AKA (= 0.013; OR = 2.833) as a primary MLEA surgery. Receiver operator curve (ROC) shows that at an ABI threshold of 0.42, the model achieves a sensitivity of 0.58 and a specificity of 0.65, yielding a Youden's J of 0.23. There was no difference in readmission, ipsilateral revision, or 5-year mortality between cohorts.DiscussionBased on our cohort of 97 patients, pre-operative ABI measurements contributed modestly to amputation level assessment within the broader clinical framework; however, ABI was not independently predictive of post-operative outcomes.

title: SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy: A propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications. RESULTS: After matching, 2,016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

title: Comparison of mid-term outcomes of different patch types for endarterectomy of the common femoral artery. Secondary analysis from the ARISTON multicentre registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to analyze patients who underwent femoral endarterectomy (FEA) for common femoral artery disease (CFAD) within the multicentre ARISTON registry aiming to compare the short-term and mid-term outcomes based on the use of different patch materials. METHODS: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicentre observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary endpoint of the study was clinically-driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). RESULTS: A total of 547 patients undergoing FEA with patch angioplasty were included in the analysis and stratified according to the patch material into three groups: (i) prosthetic patch or PP (group A, n=249), (ii) bovine pericardium patch or BPP (group B, n=262), and (iii) great saphenous vein patch or GSVP (group C, n=36). Baseline characteristics differed significantly among groups. Technical success of the FEA procedure was achieved in all cases. Perioperative mortality was low and not significantly different between groups. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from CD-TLR at two years were 86.2% (95% CI, 80.8-90.2%) in the PP group, 88.9% (95% CI, 83.1-92.8%) in the BPP group, and 69.8% (95% CI, 49.3-83.3%) in the GSVP group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (log-rank p=0.067). In multivariable analysis for freedom from CD-TLR, neither BPP (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.47-1.29; P=0.330) nor GSVP (HR 1.99, 95% CI 0.95-4.17; P=0.069) was significantly associated with the outcome. CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary multicentre real-world experience, PP and BPP were the most used materials for patch reconstruction after FEA in patients with primary CFAD. Although the distribution of baseline risk factors was different between groups, mid-term freedom from CD-TLR was not significantly different between-groups. The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

METHODS: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicentre observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary endpoint of the study was clinically-driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

title: Asymptomatic vs. Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid disease, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations. METHODS: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level one stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction, and death at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates. RESULTS: 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (IQR 6-11). SD patients had a longer median length of stay (2 vs 1 day, p = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs 36%, p = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30- and 90-day and 0.9% at 1-year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30-day, 90-day, and one year, with no difference between AD vs SD. 1-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90-day and one year, without a difference by AD vs SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer LOS, SD patients did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.
