title: Functional outcome after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury following thoracic aortic surgery.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and to assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery. METHODS: Single-centre retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024. Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was diagnosed by postoperative vocal cord paralysis. Aortic arch surgery included partial and total arch replacement, while thoracoabdominal surgery involved the proximal descending aorta. The primary endpoint was full voice recovery. Secondary endpoints included recovery of normal vocal cord mobility, residual dysphonia, the need for voice therapy, and vocal cord interventions. RESULTS: Among 2,983 patients undergoing aortic surgery, 70 (2.3%) were diagnosed with postoperative recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Median follow-up was 17 [IQR: 7-25] months. The incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was 1.7% after arch surgery and 5.3% after thoracoabdominal procedures. At final follow-up, 34 patients (50%) achieved full voice recovery, while 20 (30%) had mild dysphonia, 9 (13%) moderate dysphonia, and 5 (7%) severe dysphonia. Voice therapy was performed in 49 (70%) patients, and 10 (14%) required additional vocal cord interventions. CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury after aortic surgery was lower than previously reported. Functional outcomes were favourable, with most patients achieving full or near-complete voice recovery through conservative or interventional management. Structured follow-up and multidisciplinary care remain essential to optimize outcomes after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and to assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery. METHODS: Single-centre retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024.

title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry. METHODS: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter < 7 mm, iliac artery tortuosity index > 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention. RESULTS: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively. CONCLUSION: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD. METHODS: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy. RESULTS: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents. CONCLUSION: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.

title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on number of other specialist consultations prior to stenting (none, one, or at least two). RESULTS: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women had 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain. CONCLUSION: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment.

title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS). METHODS: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores). RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score. CONCLUSION: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS). METHODS: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation.

title: EARLY STROKE AFTER AORTIC ARCH REPAIR: COMPARATIVE AND PROPORTIONAL META-ANALYSES OF OPEN, HYBRID, AND TOTAL ENDOVASCULAR STRATEGIES.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna. Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261461659). RESULTS: 2 Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.46-8.58; P=.292; I=52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and Zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair. CONCLUSION: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly non-comparative. Treatment should be individualised according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026.

title: ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device as a Cost-Dominant Limb-Salvage Strategy for No-Option Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: A Decade and Half, Single-Centre Cohort Study with Health Economic and Q-TWiST Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) a median €88,820 per patient; long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist SCBD is lacking. METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with non-reconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary centre (January 2008-June 2025). Primary endpoints were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness versus primary amputation, and Q-TWiST. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed. FINDINGS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischaemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (HRs 1·70, 1·80, 1·71; all P ≤ ·012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = ·008). 90-day rental (€1,373/patient) reduced total expenditure six-fold versus primary amputation (€5·3M vs €30·8M), saving €76,500/patient. Q-TWiST yielded a gain of 3·37 QALYs per patient; ICER €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy. INTERPRETATION: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a six-fold reduction in costs versus primary amputation, +3·37 QALYs/patient, and an ICER of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-centre cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for non-reconstructible CLTI.

title: Continuous Site-Specific Intravascular Monitoring of Arterial and Venous Blood Oxygenation In Vivo.
abstract: Conventional pulse oximetry provides continuous non-invasive arterial oxygen saturation, whereas arterial and venous blood gas analysis provides intermittent reference measurements. Neither modality continuously monitors saturation at a selected deep intravascular site. In this proof-of-concept feasibility study, we assessed whether intravascular diffuse reflectance spectroscopy tracks the direction and time course of prespecified arterial, central venous, and regional renal venous oxygenation changes, alongside conventional pulse oximetry where an arterial comparator was appropriate.Approach. Three separate experimental protocols were performed in three pigs (one animal per protocol; n=1 per condition). Oxygen saturation was monitored with the iBLOS sensing wire in the abdominal aorta during apnea-induced systemic hypoxemia, in the inferior vena cava (IVC) during repeated hypoxic challenges, and in the right renal vein during transient venous outflow obstruction. Conventional pulse oximetry was recorded concurrently during the arterial and IVC protocols as an arterial monitoring comparator; no blood-gas samples were collected in these feasibility experiments.Main results. Continuous intravascular blood oxygenation level monitoring detected rapid and dynamic arterial desaturation and reoxygenation during systemic apnea and demonstrated reproducible responses during repeated hypoxic challenges. Venous oxygenation measured in the inferior vena cava exhibited lower baseline oxygen saturation and slower desaturation-recovery kinetics than arterial measurements, reflecting physiological oxygen extraction and circulatory transit delays. During renal vein occlusion, oxygen saturation proximal to the obstruction progressively decreased toward near-complete oxygen depletion before rapidly recovering following restoration of venous outflow. These regional physiological measurements are not feasible using peripheral pulse oximetry. Significance. This feasibility platform provides continuous, site-specific intravascular saturation trends in vascular territories that conventional non-invasive monitoring cannot directly sample. With validation against contemporaneous blood-gas measurements and evaluation in larger studies, it could help fill a monitoring gap during ischemia, reperfusion, and endovascular intervention.&#xD.

title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts. METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout. RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Brachial artery access for endovascular procedures: how safe is it?
abstract: PURPOSE: While femoral and radial artery access are routine for endovascular procedures, brachial artery access remains an important alternative in selected cases. This study aimed to evaluate the complication rate of percutaneous brachial artery access at a tertiary centre and identify potential risk factors for access-site complications. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of all procedures utilising percutaneous brachial artery access over a 12.5-year period. Patient demographics, sheath size, closure technique and complications were recorded. Complications were classified according to the CIRSE classification system. RESULTS: One hundred percutaneous brachial artery punctures were identified. Sheath sizes ranged from 3 to 9 Fr; the majority (57%) using 6 Fr. Most procedures (84%) were performed for aortic, mesenteric/renal, or peripheral arterial interventions. Overall, 23 complications occurred (23%), including 9 (9%) grade 3 complications requiring additional treatment. No convincing association was identified between complication rate and patient age, gender, or sheath size. Vascular closure devices were used in seven cases, five of which resulted in complications, including three grade 3 events. CONCLUSIONS: The complication rate associated with brachial artery access in this series was higher than that reported in much of the published literature. These findings suggest that brachial artery access may be less safe than commonly perceived and that vascular closure devices should be used with caution, particularly given their off-label status for this access site. Standardised procedural protocols and post-procedural care pathways may help reduce complication rates. Broader auditing and reporting across centres are encouraged to better define best practice.

title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis. RESULTS: The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%). CONCLUSION: Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.

Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: p p p 2 PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) (< 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m,< 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT (= 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

title: Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
abstract: AIMS/INTRODUCTION: The effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all-cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo-Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort. Lifestyle factors were assessed by questionnaire. Dietary intake was evaluated using a brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire, from which Total, Plant, and Animal low-carbohydrate diet scores were calculated. The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, or all-cause mortality. Associations were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Mean age was 51.4 ± 15.1 years, mean HbA1c was 7.9 ± 1.1%, and carbohydrate accounted for 49.3% of energy intake. During follow-up, 35 participants experienced the primary composite outcome. In multivariable Cox models, the Total LCDS (HR, 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; P = 0.012), Plant LCDS (HR, 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.94; P = 0.003), and Animal LCDS (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.87-0.996; P = 0.037) were inversely associated with the outcome. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan, low-carbohydrate dietary patterns, particularly the Plant low-carbohydrate diet score, were inversely associated with macrovascular events or all-cause mortality.

title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: P P Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures,<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort.

title: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: P P Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation.

title: Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury in the Geriatric Population: Results from the Aortic Trauma Foundation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) is evolving as the trauma population ages, yet the impact of age on treatment patterns and outcomes remains incompletely defined. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective analysis of the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry (November 2016 to November 2023) identified 823 patients with BTAI, including 118 geriatric patients (65 years and older). Demographics, injury characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes were compared between the geriatric and younger (younger than 65 years) cohorts. RESULTS: Geriatric patients more frequently presented after falls (17.8% vs 6.7%, p < 0.0001) and had a higher proportion of grade IV injuries (18.5% vs 9.2%, p = 0.0021), with no difference in admission systolic blood pressure (116 vs 116, p = 0.960) or Injury Severity Score (31 vs 33, p = 0.150). Management strategies were similar between groups, including nonoperative (37.3% vs 36.9%, p = 0.932), open (4.2% vs 1.9%, p = 0.132), and endovascular repair (58.5% vs 61.1%, p = 0.584). Despite comparable treatment approaches, geriatric patients had higher in-hospital mortality (27.1% vs 10.9%, p < 0.0001) and aortic-related mortality (8.5% vs 3.4%, p = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Geriatric patients with BTAI sustain more severe injuries and experience significantly higher mortality despite similar management strategies. These findings suggest that current treatment paradigms may not adequately address age-associated risk and highlight the need for age-specific management considerations.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis is associated with adverse events in patients with high-grade carotid artery stenosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), defined as the expansion of a subset of hematopoietic stem or progenitor cells driven by acquired mutations, represents a novel cardiovascular risk factor. Its role in patients with high-grade carotid stenosis remains to be evaluated. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) involving 30 genes implicated in CH was used as diagnostic-grade assay (SOPHiA DDM Myeloid Solution) to screen for CH in 83 prospectively collected patients with symptomatic or asymptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA). RESULTS: P interaction Clonal markers were detected in 16 (19.7 %) of 83 patients (median age 71.2 years), with prevalence increasing at advanced age. At 5-year follow-up, CH carriers showed a higher cumulative incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; P = 0.040) compared to patients without CH; all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.57). Cox regression revealed a significant association between CH and MACE in a univariable model (P = 0.047), which remained significant after multivariable adjustment for age and sex (P = 0.018). Exploratory analyses suggested that the association between CH and MACE may differ according to carotid stenosis severity, with an increased incidence of MACE observed in patients with <90 % stenosis and concomitant CH, an effect absent in patients with ≥90 % stenosis ( = 0.03). DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: CH was associated with an adverse 5-year outcome in patients with carotid artery stenosis. These findings identify CH as a hematologic contributor to post-interventional cardiovascular risk and indicate that assessment of CH may offer additional prognostic information for residual risk stratification.

title: Surgical, endovascular, and systemic management of renal cell carcinoma with intravascular recurrence.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) recurrence within the vasculature represents a rare and challenging clinical scenario with limited evidence to guide management. We report a patient with clear cell RCC and level 4 IVC thrombus who underwent successful radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy and subsequently developed disease recurrence in the supradiaphragmatic IVC and pulmonary arteries. Multidisciplinary management included novel endovascular removal of the recurrent IVC tumor followed by pulmonary bilobectomy for progressive tumor emboli. The patient remains without evidence of recurrent disease. This case highlights the complex multidisciplinary decision-making and potential role of minimally invasive endovascular techniques in managing intravascular RCC.

title: Predictors of Successful Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Match: A Texas Star Database Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to determine factors predictive of successful matching into vascular surgery residency. This has been studied in other fields, but there is a paucity of data specific to vascular surgery. This information can be helpful in guiding medical students interested in applying for this competitive field. METHODS: The Texas Seeking Transparency in Application to Residency database was used to analyze self-reported demographics, match results, and application variables from 2017 to 2025. Multiple characteristics of matched applicants were compared to unmatched applicants. Categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test, while continuous variables were assessed with nonparametric tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were performed to identify predictors of successful matches. RESULTS: A total of 170 applicants responded to the survey, 138 (81%) of whom matched. Those who matched had higher numbers of programs applied to (55 vs 46, p = 0.031), interviews offered (29 vs 20, p = 0.004), interviews attended (21 vs 13, p < 0.001), received an MD vs DO degree (82.5% vs 25%, p = 0.024), and had a vascular rotation at their home institution (85.0% vs 28.6%, p = 0.006). The number of interviews attended was the only significant predictor of matching (OR = 1.96, p = 0.021), with each additional interview attended increasing the odds of matching by 9%. The number of abstracts, posters, and presentations is independently associated with a higher number of interview offers (β = 0.86, p = 0.01), with each additional abstract, publication, or poster associated with an average increase of 0.86 interview invitations. CONCLUSIONS: This study reinforces the idea that going on more interviews increases the chances of matching. Applicants with a higher number of abstracts, posters, or presentations received more interview invites. Geographic signaling, USMLE exam scores, clerkships with honors, and honorary membership in societies were not associated with a higher chance of matching.

title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Introversion in Surgical Residency: A Risk Factor for Burnout?
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Burnout among surgical residents continues to present a critical challenge in graduate medical education. The high demands, long work hours, and intense emotional toll of surgical training make this group especially vulnerable to mental health challenges, including disengagement and exhaustion. Previous research has explored factors such as gender, training level, and work hours; however, the influence of personality traits, specifically introversion and extroversion, on burnout has been underexplored. This study seeks to bridge that gap by examining how personality influences burnout among surgical residents at a major academic institution. METHODS: This study surveyed surgical residents from a large academic medical center representing multiple surgical subspecialties and postgraduate years (PGY1-PGY7). Participants were invited to complete the survey via REDCap. The initial invitation was distributed by program directors, and subsequent reminder emails were sent directly to residents. The survey consisted of 38 items, including demographic questions and 3 validated instruments: the Big Five Inventory, a modified Big Five Inventory, and the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory. Burnout was defined as exhaustion or disengagement and classified as high, moderate, or low according to the criteria described by Demerouti et al. All statistical analyses were performed using SAS software. RESULTS: The survey was distributed to 204 trainees, and 116 responded for a response rate of 57%. Sixty-six percent of the participants identified as females and were evenly distributed across residency years. General surgery residents represented the highest number of participants (n = 20), while obstetrics and gynecology represented the fewest (n = 4). No participants reported "high" burnout on the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory scale. Higher extraversion and agreeableness scores were significantly associated with lower disengagement (r = -0.22, p < 0.05) and were not associated with exhaustion (p = 0.25). Agreeableness showed a statistically significant negative correlation with disengagement (p = 0.028). Female gender was associated with higher burnout (p < 0.01), while PGY year was insignificant. A significant difference in exhaustion and disengagement was observed across specialties (p < 0.01), with obstetrics and gynecology residents reporting the highest levels of burnout (both exhaustion and disengagement). In contrast, vascular surgery residents reported the lowest exhaustion rates, and plastic surgery residents reported the lowest disengagement rates. DISCUSSION: Our findings suggest that personality traits, particularly extraversion, may play a substantial role in how surgical residents experience burnout. Introverted residents may be more vulnerable to emotional fatigue and disengagement in high-interaction environments like surgical training. In addition to personality differences, our study also found that female residents reported significantly higher levels of exhaustion than their male peers, independent of personality traits. This gender-based difference echoes prior research highlighting the unique challenges faced by women in surgical training, including microaggressions, work-life balance pressures, imposter syndrome, and underrepresentation in leadership roles. Interestingly, PGY year was not a significant factor for burnout in our analysis, contrasting several earlier studies that reported increased burnout among junior residents. These findings highlight the need for personality-informed wellness interventions and support systems that align with residents' coping styles and psychological needs. CONCLUSION: Personality traits are associated with burnout in surgical residency. Specifically, extroversion may be protective against disengagement. Residency programs should consider integrating personality assessments into onboarding and wellness initiatives to better support residents at risk, particularly introverts and female trainees.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Burnout among surgical residents continues to present a critical challenge in graduate medical education. The high demands, long work hours, and intense emotional toll of surgical training make this group especially vulnerable to mental health challenges, including disengagement and exhaustion. Previous research has explored factors such as gender, training level, and work hours; however, the influence of personality traits, specifically introversion and extroversion, on burnout has been underexplored.

title: Rare common femoral vein adventitial cystic disease presenting with lower-extremity swelling.
abstract: Adventitial cystic disease (ACD) is a rare, nonatherosclerotic disorder caused by mucin-filled cysts within the vessel wall that produce luminal compression. Venous ACD is uncommon and may mimic deep vein thrombosis. A 24-year-old woman presented with right leg pain and swelling from a 2.8-cm common femoral vein cyst. The patient underwent cyst excision and bovine patch venoplasty but developed postoperative thrombosis from venoplasty-site stenosis and hematoma compression. Thrombectomy and angioplasty failed, requiring venous stenting. Pathology confirmed ACD. The patient recovered on enoxaparin and clopidogrel. This case emphasizes confirming durable venous outflow after cyst excision.

title: Unexpected para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak: A technical pitfall.
abstract: We report an unusual case of para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair. Preprocedural computed tomography and angiography demonstrated no venous communication. During progressive NBCA injection, sequential opacification of the fourth lumbar vein and a para-aortic venous structure became apparent, prompting immediate cessation of embolization. The patient remained asymptomatic, and follow-up imaging demonstrated stable aneurysm size without complications. This case highlights a rare technical pitfall and emphasizes careful fluoroscopic monitoring during NBCA sac embolization despite initially negative imaging findings.

title: Methylene blue-guided parenchyma-sparing ex vivo resection and autotransplantation for a type III renal arteriovenous fistula with large renal vein aneurysm: A technical case report.
abstract: High-flow renal arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), type III with vein aneurysms, are rare and often require nephrectomy. A 54-year-old man presented with lumbar pain and hematuria. Computed tomography angiography revealed an 8- × 12-cm right renal vein aneurysm and a type III arteriovenous fistula occupying >30% of the kidney. After ex vivo nephrectomy with cold perfusion, selective methylene blue injection delineated the AVM nidus and parenchyma, guiding resection and excision. The procedure was performed by a multidisciplinary team including a vascular surgeon, transplant surgeon, and urologist. The kidney was reconstructed and reimplanted. Postoperative creatinine levels stabilized at 1.10 mg/dL, and computed tomography angiography confirmed AVM exclusion and preserved perfusion. Methylene blue mapping can enable parenchyma-sparing repair in selected cases.

title: Intravascular ultrasound-guided repair of delayed traumatic popliteal artery occlusion using an interwoven nitinol stent.
abstract: Traumatic popliteal artery occlusion is a limb-threatening condition traditionally managed with open surgical revascularization. Here, we describe a 66-year-old man with delayed occlusion after high-energy lower-extremity trauma. Initial computed tomography angiography indicated preserved flow despite severe arterial deformation. Progressive heel necrosis developed after fracture fixation and debridement; repeat imaging on day 24 showed complete occlusion of the popliteal artery. Intravascular ultrasound-guided endovascular repair with an interwoven nitinol stent restored antegrade flow. Wound healing was achieved after flap and skin graft procedures, and stent patency was maintained for >2.5 years.

title: Anesthesia and the Periprocedural Management of Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke Treated with Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion and has markedly improved functional outcomes. While procedural sedation was historically favored instead of general anesthesia due to safety concerns, current evidence does not support superior functional outcomes with procedural sedation compared with protocol-driven general anesthesia. General anesthesia is associated with higher reperfusion rates; however, strict hemodynamic control-particularly avoidance of hypotension-and ventilatory management are critical to preserving cerebral perfusion and improving outcomes. Ongoing trials are expected to clarify optimal anesthetic strategies in both anterior and posterior circulation strokes. In the meantime, the choice between general anesthesia and procedural sedation should consider patient-specific characteristics, procedural complexity, and institutional expertise. Future research should focus on better defining patient selection or stroke subtypes most likely to benefit from general anesthesia or procedural sedation, hemodynamic management, and neuroprotective strategies to maximize reperfusion, minimize complications, and improve recovery.

title: Laser cryo-sclerotherapy versus conventional sclerotherapy for reticular veins and telangiectasias: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the hybrid laser cryo-sclerotherapy (LCS; Nd:Y-AG 1064 nm + 75% hypertonic glucose [HG]) protocol produces superior aesthetic outcomes compared with combined conventional sclerotherapy (CS: 67.5% glucose + 0.3% polidocanol [POL]) for the treatment of lower limb reticular veins and telangiectasias (CEAP C1). METHODS: For this single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial, 60 patients were assessed for eligibility; 4 did not provide informed consent and were not randomized. A total of 56 female patients with CEAP C1 disease and Fitzpatrick phototypes I-III were randomized, with only one lower limb treated per participant: 32 to the LCS group (Nd:YAG 1064 nm + HG75%) and 24 to the CS group (HG67.5% + POL0.3%). Two participants who underwent LCS were subsequently lost to follow-up between Day 1 and Day 30; 54 participants (30 and 24 from the LCS and CS groups, respectively) completed the 90-day follow-up and were analyzed per protocol. Standardized photographs were obtained on Day 1, Day 30, and Day 90, with and without augmented reality (AR; VeinViewer Flex), and were assessed by two blinded external vascular physicians using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS). Complications, residual pigmentation, and quality of life (Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire) were evaluated as secondary end points. RESULTS: Both groups had equivalent baseline characteristics. The LCS group was superior to the CS group in all GAIS outcomes: D1→D90 without AR (P = .026; r = 0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.04-0.58; moderate effect); D1→D90 with AR (P < .001; r = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.28-0.72; large effect); D30→D90 without AR (P < .001; r = 0.56; 95% CI, 0.31-0.74; large effect); D30→D90 with AR (P < .001; r = 0.52; 95% CI, 0.26-0.71; large effect). After Bonferroni correction for these four primary comparisons (α = .0125), the D1→D90 comparison without AR no longer reached significance, whereas the remaining three comparisons did. Temporal analysis revealed a progressive late aesthetic response in the LCS group; 80.0% of participants continued improving between Day 30 and Day 90 vs 29.1% in the CS group (70.8% with No Change). The ecchymosis duration was significantly shorter in the LCS group (median, 5.0 vs 10.0 days; P = .012). Severe pigmentation on Day 90 was observed exclusively in the CS group (8.3% vs 0%; P = .019; r = 0.22; small effect; power = 36.4%; this finding is exploratory, see the Discussion section). No cases of deep vein thrombosis or ulcer occurred. Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire score improvement was significant in both groups (P < .001), with no intergroup difference. Inter-rater agreement was substantial to near-perfect for GAIS assessments (κ = 0.735-0.913) and perfect for complication grading (κ = 1.000). CONCLUSIONS: The LCS protocol was superior to CS in all GAIS outcomes, with moderate-to-large effect sizes and consistent inter-rater agreement. The aesthetic response was progressive, consolidating between Day 30 and Day 90, with the largest effect size in the late period. AR amplified the magnitude of the detected effects and improved inter-rater agreement, reinforcing its role as a standardizing tool in aesthetic phlebology randomized controlled trials. These statistical findings should be weighed against the higher costs and complexity of LCS relative to CS in a purely cosmetic CEAP C1 population (see the Discussion section).

title: Early-term and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion of high-risk subacute and early chronic residual dissection after type A repair.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Late mortality, progressive aneurysmal degeneration, and major reinterventions remain frequent after repair of type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to evaluate early- and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion in patients with high-risk residual dissection treated during the subacute or early chronic phase. METHODS: This study was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional database. All consecutive patients undergoing endovascular completion for high-risk residual aortic dissection after type A dissection repair between January 2017 and September 2025 were included. Completion was performed using thoracic endovascular aortic repair alone or combined with the stented-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination technique when distal extension exceeded Ishimaru zone 5. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and morbidity, as well as 3- and 5-year survival and reintervention rates. RESULTS: Among 127 patients surviving initial type A repair, 48 (37.8%) underwent endovascular completion (subacute n = 33; early chronic n = 15). No 30-day deaths occurred, and technical success was achieved in all cases. Major adverse events occurred in 6.2%, with no spinal cord ischemia. Five patients (10.4%) required early reintervention. Median clinical follow-up was 54 months. Estimated survival was 97.9% at 3 years and 90.3% at 5 years. Freedom from major reintervention was 93.5% at 3 years and 89.1% at 5 years. False lumen thrombosis was achieved in 89.6% of thoracic and 81.4% of visceral segments. CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular completion of high-risk residual dissection after type A repair is safe and effective, providing excellent midterm survival, low major reintervention rates, and high rates of aortic remodeling.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Late mortality, progressive aneurysmal degeneration, and major reinterventions remain frequent after repair of type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to evaluate early- and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion in patients with high-risk residual dissection treated during the subacute or early chronic phase. METHODS: This study was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional database.

title: Trends in Surgical Specialty Fellowship Applications in the Era of COVID-19 and Virtual Interviewing.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted surgical training by decreasing operative volume and changing resident exposure to various specialties. Simultaneously, fellowship interviewing transitioned from in-person to virtual formats. The effect of the pandemic on surgical fellowship application trends has not been assessed. This study characterizes surgical fellowship application trends surrounding the COVID-19 pandemic. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study using publicly available fellowship application and match data. SETTING: Data from the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) and Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS). PARTICIPANTS: Applicants to colon and rectal surgery (CRS), surgical oncology, pediatric surgery, surgical critical care (SCC), thoracic surgery, and vascular surgery fellowships from 2017 to 2024. RESULTS: The total number of surgical fellowship applicants increased by 19%, from 748 in 2017 to 890 in 2024. The largest increase in applicants occurred in 2020 after the start of virtual interviews, particularly for SCC (+27.0%). The number of submitted applications across all specialties increased by an average of 37.4% during the study period, with notable growth after the pandemic began. However, in the 2023 to 2024 cycle when virtual interviews were no longer mandated, overall application numbers decreased (-3.0%) and the number of total applicants to subspecialty fellowships decreased (-4.4%). Match percentages increased that cycle for all specialties except CRS and surgical oncology. CONCLUSIONS: While the number of surgical fellowship applications and applicants increased overall throughout the study period, stark increases occurred both immediately after the pandemic's onset and when virtual interviews began. Early declines in both the number of applicants and applications submitted after the return of in-person interviews suggests that interview format may influence recruitment patterns, which has important implications for both fellowship programs and applicants.

title: Hot wire technique for septal fenestration in chronic type B aortic dissection: A case report.
abstract: Persistent false lumen in chronic type B aortic dissection complicates endovascular repair. The hot wire technique offers a precise method for septal fenestration, enabling endovascular treatment when standard approaches are not feasible. We present a case of a 65-year-old man with prior ascending aorta replacement and elephant trunk, who developed a large descending aortic aneurysm with residual dissection and a false lumen in which the elephant trunk resided, prohibiting conventional thoracic endovascular aortic repair. Septal fenestration allowing continuous flow was created using the hot wire technique, demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of this technique in complex chronic dissections with challenging anatomy.

title: Hybrid pin penetration open stent technique: Retrospective study of a new approach to frozen elephant trunk procedure.
abstract: Total arch replacement using the frozen elephant trunk technique for acute type A aortic dissection involving the aortic arch remains technically demanding because of complex supra-aortic branch reconstruction and prolonged circulatory arrest. We developed a modified fenestrated open stent technique, termed the hybrid pin-penetration open stent (HIPPOS) technique, to simplify branch reconstruction while minimizing supra-aortic vessel manipulation. We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients who underwent total arch replacement using HIPPOS between May 2024 and May 2026 at a single institution by a single surgeon. Following deployment of a Frozenix open stent graft (Japan Lifeline), antegrade fenestrations were created under direct vision using needle penetration and sequential dilation, followed by reconstruction with balloon-expandable covered stent grafts. All procedures were successfully completed. Operative durations decreased with increasing numbers of fenestrations, reflecting procedural refinement and the surgical learning curve. Two perioperative deaths occurred in patients with profound preoperative shock, and one patient experienced a nondisabling stroke. No postoperative hoarseness, paraplegia, fenestration-related endoleak, or distal stent-induced new entry was observed. Follow-up computed tomography angiography confirmed satisfactory graft conformability and durable branch patency. HIPPOS is a reproducible modification of the frozen elephant trunk procedure with encouraging early clinical outcomes.

title: Hybrid approach with thoracic endovascular treatment and abdominal aortic replacement for acute type B aortic dissection complicated by ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: The coexistence of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and acute aortic dissection is an unusual and life-threatening condition. We present the case of a patient who underwent simultaneous thoracic endovascular aortic repair and graft replacement for synchronous acute type B aortic dissection and ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. After deployment of the stent graft at the distal arch, graft replacement was accomplished without hemodynamic deterioration. The true lumen of the infrarenal abdominal aorta expanded, and a secure proximal anastomosis was achieved. A hybrid approach can be considered when different aortic diseases involve the same aortic lesion in an emergent setting.

title: AA amyloidosis in the four historical monogenic autoinflammatory diseases: Clinical burden and insights from a retrospective referral-centre study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: AA amyloidosis (AAA) remains a life-threatening yet largely preventable complication of monogenic autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs). METHODS: We retrospectively described patients with AAA secondary to one of the four historical monogenic AIDs (familial Mediterranean fever [FMF], cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome [CAPS], mevalonate kinase deficiency [MKD] and tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome [TRAPS]) followed at the French National Referral Centre for Monogenic AIDs and Inflammatory Amyloidosis (2012-2025). RESULTS: Among 181 patients followed for AAA, 50 (28%) had one of the four monogenic AIDs (FMF n = 41, CAPS n = 4, MKD n = 3, TRAPS n = 2), corresponding to an overall prevalence of 5% among all patients with monogenic AIDs. AAA preceded the diagnosis of the underlying AID in 40% of patients, particularly those with non-FMF diseases. Disease burden remained high, with 46% of patients requiring kidney transplantation, whereas mortality reached 26% during follow-up. CONCLUSION: AAA continues to reflect delayed diagnosis, highlighting the need for increased awareness among adult healthcare providers, systematic genetic evaluation of unexplained AAA and early inflammatory control.
